findings.title: Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version
findings.body: OptimizedImage now defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and again at line 149 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so any existing caller passing separate width and height arguments will raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and the line-145 implementation is dead code. The width/height API must be kept working or all callers updated/removed deliberately.

findings.title: Percentage downsize breaks animated GIF handling
findings.body: The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). When allow_animation is true and the file is a GIF, OptimizedImage.optimize dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimensions to gifsicle as --resize-fit. Gifsicle expects WxH dimensions, not "80%" (the value also gets a trailing \> from the non-animated path conventions), so it will fail to resize animated GIFs. The loop then retries the failing operation up to 5 times and the oversized GIF proceeds to Upload.create_for still over the limit, so large animated uploads are not actually downsized.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the same file is used as input and output
findings.body: The resizing loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize and uses tempfile.path as both source and destination. If convert/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, unsupported format such as SVG, unsupported geometry), convert_with returns false but the loop still runs up to 5 expensive attempts and then uploads whatever is left at that path. Using the same path for input and output also risks truncating/corrupting the only copy of the uploaded tempfile if the external tool fails part-way, and for non-animated GIFs the [0] selector in downsize_instructions silently reduces the image to its first frame. Failures should be checked and the resize should go through a separate temporary output file that replaces the original only on success.

findings.title: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings and upload type
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], respecting different configured limits for images vs attachments. It now hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for every file type. Sites with a lower max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb will let users select files the server will reject, and sites configured above 10MB will incorrectly block uploads they intend to allow. The same regression is repeated in displayErrorForUpload at line 246, which reports 10MB as the limit on a 413 response regardless of the actual configured/server limit.

findings.title: Remote download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypasses configured image limit before validation
findings.body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs previously capped the download at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes; it now always allows 10.megabytes. Combined with the new in-request downsizing, an API caller can force the server to download and run up to 5 ImageMagick/ImageOptim passes over a 10MB untrusted image even on sites whose configured max_image_size_kb is much smaller, increasing bandwidth/CPU (decompression-bomb) exposure. If the image still exceeds max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts it is only then rejected by normal upload validation, after the expensive work has been done.
